newsitem.title: USA: WLR Foods takes Q3 charge to battle turkey disease.
newsitem.headline: WLR Foods takes Q3 charge to battle turkey disease.

text.p: WLR Foods Inc, the nation's second largest turkey producer, took a $1.5 million third quarter charge to combat a deadly turkey disease, the company said.

WLR Foods said the charge related to cutting its North Carolina turkey flock by one-third this summer to curb the spread of poult enteritis and mortality syndrome (PEMS), a disease that attacks young turkeys.
"We don't have a significant increase in mortality this year," said WLR Foods spokeswoman Gail Price. She said the disease is most deadly from May to September.
WLR Foods reported a third quarter loss of $9.6 million, largely due to lower turkey prices and higher feed costs.
PEMS, discovered in 1991, killed some two million North Carolina turkeys in both 1995 and 1996. About half of the infected birds die and survivors are weak and in poor health.
WLR said in March it cut turkey production at 45 of its 151 farms in North Carolina because of previous losses it incurred from the disease.
"Common sense would tell you we should have a better situation with the reduced birds," Price said.
State and university scientists have recommended strict security measures at poultry farms this year to slow the spread of the disease.

"The main effort is to beef up bio-security. You should not be able to walk onto a farm," said Jean-Pierre Vaillancourt, associate professor of poultry health management at North Carolina State University.
Laboratory tests suggest darkling beetles, chickens and flies are carriers, but this theory has not been tested on turkey farms, said Vaillancourt.
PEMS is not harmful to humans.
